collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — JUSTICE AND CONSEQUENCES (JUS-01 to JUS-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Everyday rules, disputes between neighbors, the elders and the council, making things right, losing a role, a night to cool down, wrongful suspicion and evidence that doesn't add up. Consequences are proportionate and never cruel; children get guidance; nobody goes without food, water or shelter; an accusation is not guilt.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager pressed a neighbor into trading their good spear, and now the neighbor wants it back: ask the elders, or talk it over.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: For a week, (subject) kept asking (friend) to trade (friend.his/her) good fishing spear for a basket of shells and a carved comb, a little more insistently every day. In the end (friend) said yes, just to make it stop. Now (friend.he/she) wants the spear back. (subject) says a trade is a trade.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The elders ask (friend) whether (friend.he/she) wanted to trade. "No. I wanted (subject.him/her) to stop asking." The elders say that a trade made only to end the asking isn't a fair trade, and ask them to swap back. (subject) is cross, and says (friend) should have said no. (friend) says (friend.he/she) did, six times. The elders agree with (friend).

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) finds (subject). "I said yes to make you stop asking. That isn't the same as wanting to." (subject) is quiet for a moment. "...I did ask a lot." (subject.He/she) gives back the spear, and (friend) gives back the shells and the comb. Things are a little awkward for a while. Then (subject) asks to borrow the spear, just once, and asks only once.
